locator: §4.1, 'Schroeder (2008b, 2008c) dubs the distinction between inconsistencies that involve one attitude-type directed towards inconsistent contents, A-type inconsistencies'
interpretation: Schroeder's cost argument as the entry reports it: complex sentences 'express attitudes that don't reduce to the attitudes which would be expressed by either conjunct', so expressivism needs new attitude types and rules for each, and must explain inconsistency by incoherence between attitude types (B-type), while 'the clearest examples of genuine inconsistency' are A-type, which he takes as a reason to prefer an A-type model if non-cognitivists could build one. Recorded as an attack on constant-meaning expressivism, not as a refutation. Attribution reading on a secondary witness: the claim records the position the entry reports, not a thesis of the entry's author. No primary text is pinnable (in copyright, no immutable open text).
